style_instructions: Speak every supplied word exactly, in order, without adding, omitting, repeating or paraphrasing anything. This is one continuous personal thought shared with a familiar person through your phone's selfie camera. Keep the everyday contractions exactly as written. Say AI as its letters and GTM as its letters, then Engine; these are ordinary references in the thought, not announcements. The overall pace is brisk and connected, around sixty-five to seventy seconds for the complete passage, without rushing or stretching to hit a time. Move lightly through connecting words and let meaning change the rhythm. Use clearly audible but believable and irregular pitch, pace and emphasis variations: sometimes a curious lift, sometimes easy settling, a brief quick run through an obvious point, then a small space when the thought changes. Avoid repeating the same rise-and-fall pattern in every sentence. Keep the voice comfortably close and ordinarily projected, alive and interested rather than subdued or flat. Start with reflective, matter-of-fact self-recognition; the admission about getting better is candid rather than apologetic. Explain the engine as something you are still working out, with interested energy rather than a product pitch. Let the questions sound genuinely curious and give their final words room to finish. The line about a hobby has light, faintly amused acceptance, without an added laugh or an announcer punchline. End by asking people a real question, casually open and interested, with the final word fully spoken and a brief natural quiet ending. Keep pauses proportionate to the thought: short within clauses, slightly longer at real turns, with no dramatic silence after every line. Do not sound like a narrator, presenter, commercial, motivational speech or polished radio read. No sing-song phrasing, theatrical voice, imitation of someone else, fake stumbles, fillers, added breaths for effect, laughter, ambience, effects or music. Do not speak these directions.
